name: Rime: Live Captions
oneLine: A free iPhone app from Aarhus that calls itself a hørebrille: speech becomes large captions, with Danish and English translation, all on the phone, offline after a one-time download, with no account and nothing saved.

platforms.detail: The website calls it a free app for iPhone, and the App Store lists it for iPhone only, not iPad. No Google Play listing was found.

deviceRequirements.detail: It needs an iPhone with iOS 26 or later.

roomCaptions.detail: Speech around you becomes large text on the screen as it happens, while the app is open and listening.

groupConversations.text: Listening range: close, table or room
groupConversations.detail: In settings you choose how far Rime listens: only the person sitting close, the whole table or everything in the room. Its pages don't describe telling speakers apart.

languages.detail: Rime listens for Danish by default; when people speak English, you choose English under Language spoken.

offline.detail: Captions use Apple's speech recognition on the iPhone. The first time, the iPhone downloads the language model (and the translation model if you translate); after that Rime doesn't go online.

speakerLabels.detail: Rime's pages don't describe showing who is talking.

speakerDirection.detail: Rime lets you set how far it listens, but doesn't describe showing where a voice comes from.

translation.text: Danish and English, both ways, offline
translation.detail: Pick the language you read and Rime translates what is said in the other language, line by line. Translation runs on the iPhone and works without internet after a one-time download.

saveTranscripts.text: No, text is gone when you close the app
saveTranscripts.detail: Nothing from the conversation is saved: the text disappears when you close the app. Rime only remembers settings such as text size and listening range.

export.detail: Nothing from the conversation is saved, and Rime's pages don't describe copying or sharing captions.

fileUpload.detail: Rime's pages describe live captions from the microphone, not transcribing files.

display.text: Large text, size in several steps
display.detail: Make the text bigger or smaller with one tap, in several steps. Grey text is still being written and white text is done, and the newest line always stays at the bottom.

soundAlerts.detail: Rime's pages don't describe alerts for sounds like a doorbell or an alarm.

phoneCalls.detail: Rime's pages describe conversations with people around you, not phone calls.

humanCaptioners.detail: Captions and translations are made automatically and can contain mistakes.

privacy.text: On the phone; nothing sent or saved
privacy.detail: Speech recognition (Apple's, on the iPhone) and translation run on the phone. Audio is not recorded, stored or sent, there is no analytics or tracking, and the App Store privacy label says no data is collected.

account.detail: There is no account, no ads and no tracking.

availability.detail: Found on the Danish App Store only, not in the US, UK, German, Swedish, Norwegian, Finnish, Dutch or Icelandic stores (November 2026). The app itself is in Danish and English.

freePlan.detail: Rime is free on the App Store with no in-app purchases and no ads.

price.detail: The Danish App Store lists Rime as free with no in-app purchases (November 2026).

accessibilityFunding.detail: No public programme is described; the app is free.

strengths.text: Free with no in-app purchases, no account, no ads and no tracking.
Speech recognition and translation run on the iPhone, so nothing said leaves the phone and nothing is saved.
Translates between Danish and English line by line, and keeps working without internet after a one-time download.
You choose how far it listens: the person sitting close, the whole table or everything in the room.

limits.text: Needs an iPhone with iOS 26 or later; the App Store lists it for iPhone only.
Captions Danish and English only, and listens for Danish unless you switch Language spoken to English.
Nothing is saved: the text disappears when you close the app.

quotes: They talk. You read along. Everything stays on the phone.
In Danish we call it a hørebrille: like reading glasses, but for conversations.
At dinner, someone talks fast, someone switches to English, and the thread is gone.
It never leaves the phone, and no audio or text is saved. Free, no account.

notes: Developer: the App Store seller is Thorbjørn BakJensen (Aarhus, per the App Store trader details); the website says Rime is made by Bona (Bona.city, part of TBJ Consult, CVR 45933156). Versions: 1.0 on 11 Oct 2026, 1.2 on 18 Oct (Danish and English translation, English interface, text size steps), 1.2.1 on 22 Oct. Conflict: the privacy policy (8 Oct 2026, before translation and English were added) mentions only Apple's Danish language pack and a translation model; the App Store listing (1.2.1) says the iPhone downloads the language and translation models from Apple the first time. Both say nothing is sent afterwards. Platforms: the App Store page says 'Only for iPhone'; its compatibility section also lists Apple silicon Macs and Apple Vision for the iPhone app ('Designed for iPhone. Not verified for macOS.'), not counted. A Google Play search for 'Rime live captions' (Denmark, November 2026) shows no app from Bona or Thorbjørn BakJensen, and the website says 'Gratis app til iPhone'. The website's waitlist text mentions glasses with captions that may come later; not counted as a feature. Not found: speaker labels, custom words, summaries, export, file transcription, sound alerts, phone or video calls, sign language. Availability: the lookup API returned the app for Denmark only among dk, se, no, de, gb, fi, nl, is and us. The website's text is filled in by its script (lang.js); the Danish and English texts were read from it. All pages opened 2026-11-02 with curl.
